entities.summary: Marinus of Tyre was a Greek-speaking Phoenician Roman geographer, cartographer and mathematician who founded mathematical geography and provided the underpinnings of Claudius Ptolemy's influential Geography. Born in the 1st century CE, his exact birthdate is unknown, in the Roman province of Phoenicia, modern-day Lebanon. This region was a hub of ancient trade and learning, with the Phoenicians being renowned for their seafaring prowess and merchant networks. Marinus' work built upon existing knowledge of astronomy and mathematics, incorporating new discoveries from the ancient Greeks and Babylonians. He was particularly interested in the measurement of the Earth's circumference, a concept that was still a topic of debate among scholars at the time. Marinus' contributions to geography and mathematics were widely recognized during his lifetime, and his work had a lasting impact on the development of cartography and scientific inquiry. As a key figure in the transmission of knowledge from ancient Greece to Rome, Marinus of Tyre played a significant role in shaping the intellectual landscape of the ancient world. His work has been rediscovered and reevaluated in recent years, highlighting the importance of mathematical geography in understanding the historical context of ancient Roman society.
